questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

The Chairman of the company ordered all of the employees (1)/ to refrain for making long personal calls during (2)/ working hours in order to boost productivity. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 1**

 [IMAGE: https://lh5.googleusercontent.com/vA4Z-MyppkGwoS0KM3dppwc3Fv6OQHoSAya4uUmQXIiZQS0OmypbFFv4LGfdYMOtmTeICNyWKmf11bF-9IN69xESiQxNlOpil3I32QOJlv6hDcJIU_d2mvhzS-tYfotlFbHxlawE]

• In the above sentence use "from" instead of preposition "for"
 
• **NOTE:**__ Verb refrain is always followed by preposition "from"

• Different from
 
• Abstain from
 
• Borrow from
 
• Derive from
 
• Dissuade from
 
• Prevent from
 
• Prohibit from
 
• Recover from
 
• Refrain from
 
• Debar from
 
• Deter from

questions.solution:

**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

I write ______ my sister every month.
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 3**

Here, concept of preposition is brought under consideration.

Let's find out the uses of all the given options :-

In - Used to describe the position of someone or something in an enclosed area or place surrounding it.

Of - Used for belonging to, relating to, or connected with someone or something; to indicate reference.

To - Used when there is a specific destination in mind.

At - Used for precise times.

With reference to the context, letter is written to her sister. Hence, preposition **to **should be used here. Thus, option 3 i.e. **to **is the correct answer.

**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

States desperately trying to better their socio-economic report cards don’t need (those) kind of psychological dampener.
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 1**

Here, concept of demonstrative pronoun is brought under consideration. Pronouns that point to specific things: this, that, these, and those, as in “This is an apple,” “Those are boys,” or “Take these to the clerk.” The same words are used as demonstrative adjectives when they modify noun

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

The apex court has directed that (their) is a need to bring in mechanism in the Government function to make it transparent.
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 3**

The verb used after bracket word is a singular verb. And, we know that **these **and **those **are demonstrative pronouns. And, they are used to denote plural noun. That is, plural verb to be used with them. Hence, options 1 & 2 are eliminated. Also, **their **is used as an object pronoun, at the end of the sentence. Hence, option 4 is eliminated. So, option 3 i.e. **there **is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence - **The apex court has directed that there is a need to bring in mechanism in the Government function to make it transparent.

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.**

Low education means

P: to the poverty and

Q: gender inequality in the society

R: low employment which leads
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 1**

Clearly, the sentence doesn't end with a conjunction. Hence, option 3 is eliminated. Now, Q ends with a noun, and R starts with a noun. Hence, two nouns do not come together. Thus, sequence QR is not correct. Hence, option 2 is the correct answer. Now, R ends with a verb i.e. **leads **that has conjunction before it. Hence, it needs an object. So, the sentence cannot end with a verb. Hence, option 4 is eliminated. Thus, option 1 i.e. **RPQ **is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence - **Low education means low employment which leads to the poverty and gender inequality in the society.

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.**

We should stop

P: the quality of water

Q: usage properly and maintain

R: misusing water, manage water
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 4**

Here, we can only apply logic to the jumbled sentence. The starter of the sentence describes that we should stop, now a quality of a sentence is not stopped. Also, it is not defined in Q, what should be stopped. Hence, the starter will not be followed by P or Q. Hence, options 2 & 3 are eliminated. Now, sequence RP is grammatically incorrect. Hence, option 1 is also eliminated. So, option 4 i.e. **RQP ** is the correct answer.

**Correct sequence - **We should stop misusing water, manage water usage properly and maintain the quality of water.

questions.question: There are 50 building in a row. Green building is 14th from right end. What is its position from the left end?
questions.solution:
According to the given information:

Total number of building in a row = 50

Position of Green Building from the right end = 14th

So, the Position of the green building from the left end = 50 - 14 + 1 = 37th

Hence, the position of the Green building from the left end is 37th.

questions.question: The present ages of P and Q are in ratio 3 : 5. 6 years ago the sum of their ages was 52 years. What is the present age (in years) of Q?
questions.solution:
Let x years be the present age of P & y years be the present age of Q.

The ratio of present ages is → x/y = 3/5 → 5x - 3y= 0 …. Equation (1)

Then, Before 6 years

Age of P = x - 6

Age of Q = y - 6

The sum of their ages is → x + y = 64 …… Equation (2)

By solving equation (1) and equation (2) we get:

x = 24 & y = 40.

Hence, the present age of Q is 40 years.

questions.question: In a certain code language, "SALE" is written as "35" and "FLAT" is written as "37". How is "TAKE" written in that code language?
questions.solution:
As per the alphabetical positions of the letters;

F + L + A + T = 6 + 12 + 1 + 20 = 39 - 2 = 37 (given)

Similarly,

T + A + K + E = 20 + 1 + 11 + 5 = 37 - 2 = 35

Hence, **“TAKE”** written in that code language as **“35”**.

questions.question: How many numbers are there from 14 to 159 which are divisible by both 2 and 8?
questions.solution:
The numbers which are divisible by 8 are also divisible by 2.

Therefore, the numbers divisible by 8 between 14 and 159: 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64, 72, 80, 88, 96, 104, 112, 120, 128, 136, 144, 152 (18 numbers)

**Alternate method∶**

The first number divisible by 8 after 14 is 16 and the number which is divisible by 8 and smaller than 159 is 152.

Last term = First term + (n - 1) × Difference

⇒ 152 = 16 + (n - 1) × 8

⇒ n = 18

L alone can complete a work in 200 hours. M alone can complete the same work in 150 hours. L, M and N together can complete the same work in 60 hours. In how many hours can N alone complete the work?
questions.solution:
Let efficiencies of L, M and N be l, m and n respectively.

One-day efficiency of L : l = 1/200

One-day efficiency of M : m = 1/150

Combined one-day efficiency : l + m + n = 1/60

Substituting values of l and m, we get

1/200 + 1/150 + 1/n = 1/60

1/n = 1/60 - 1/150 - 1/200 = (10 - 4 - 3)/600 = 3/600 = 1/200

∴ N can do the work in 200 hours.

questions.question: Mukesh and Dinesh together can complete a work in 120 days. Mukesh alone can complete the work in 150 days. In how many days can Dinesh alone complete the work?
questions.solution:
Let efficiencies of Mukesh and Dinesh be m and d.

One-day efficiency of Mukesh: m = 1/150

Combined one-day efficiency: m + d = 1/120

Substituting value of m, we get

1/150 + d = 1/120

d = 1/120 - 1/150 = (5 - 4)/600 = 1/600

Therefore, Dinesh can do the work in 600 days

questions.question: An article has marked price of Rs. 7600 and is available at a discount of 15%. The shopkeeper gives another discount to the buyer and sells the article for Rs. 5814. What is the second discount (in %) offered?
questions.solution:
**Short Trick:**

Selling price of article after 1st discount = 85/100 × 7600 = Rs. 6460

Second discount percentage = (6460 - 5814)/6460 × 100

= 646/6460 × 100 = 10%

Detailed Solution:

Cost after first discount: 7600 - 15% = 7600 - 15 × 7600/100

= 7600 - 1140 = Rs. 6460

Let second discount be d%

Cost after second discount = 6460 - 6460 × d/100

= 6460(1 - d/100) = 5814

Solving for d, we get

1 - d/100 = 5814/6460 = 0.9

d/100 = 1 - 0.9 = 0.1

d = 10%

Ratio of MP to SP = m/(21 m/25) = 25/21

questions.question: Of three positive numbers, the ratio of first and second is 5 : 6 and that of second and third is 9 : 1. The product of first and third number is 480. What is the sum of the three numbers?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ratio of first and second number = 5 : 6

Ratio of second and third number = 9 : 1

Product of 1st and 3rd number is 480

All three numbers are positive

**Concept Used:**

Concept of ratio and proportion

**Calculation:**

Let, the first two numbers be 5x and 6x.

Second Number : Third Number = 9 : 1

⇒ 2nd number / 3rd number = 9/1

⇒ 3rd number = 2nd number/9

⇒ 3rd number = 6x/9 = 2x/3

Accordingly,

5x × 2x/3 = 480

⇒ (10/3)x² = 480

⇒ x² = 48 × 3

⇒ x = 12 [∵ All numbers are positive, negative value of x should be neglated]

Sum of numbers = 5x + 6x + 2x/3

⇒ 11x + 2x/3

⇒ 11 × 12 + (2 × 12)/3

⇒ 132 + 8

⇒ 140

**∴ The sum of three numbers is 140**

questions.question: Average of 10 consecutive even numbers is 11. Which number is the smallest of the 10 numbers?
questions.solution:
Let the first number be 2x.

Sum of 10 consecutive numbers starting from 2x : 2x + (2x + 2) + (2x + 4) + ........ + (2x + 18) = (10 × 2x) + (2 + 4 + 6 + ... + 18) = 20x + 2(1 + 2 + ... + 9) = 20x + 2(9 × 10/2) (Sum of first n natural numbers = n × (n + 1)/2)

Average: (20x + 9 × 10)/10 = 2x + 9 = 11

→ x = 1

Smallest number: 2x = 2

A man spends 75% of his income and saves the rest. If his income increases by 50% and spending increases by 80%, then what is the percentage change in his savings?
questions.solution:
Let the old salary be s.

Expenditure = 75% = 3s/4

Savings = 25% = s/4

New Expenditure = 3s/4 + 80% = 3s/4 × (1 + 80/100) = 3s/4 × (9/5) = 27s/20.

questions.question: The downstream speed of a boat is 42 km/hr and the speed of current is 3 km/hr. What is the total time (in hours) taken by the boat to cover 72 km upstream and 84 km downstream?
questions.solution:
Let the speed of boat and current be b and c km/hr respectively.

Downstream speed = b + c = 42 km/hr

Speed of current = c = 3 km/hr

⇒ Speed of boat = 42 - 3 = 39 km/hr.

Time taken to go upstream: d/s = 72/(39 - 3) = 72/36 = 2 hrs

Time taken to go downstream: d/s = 84/42 = 2 hrs.

Total time: 2 + 2 = 4 hrs

Time taken to return: d/10

Total time taken: d/5 + d/10 = 3d/10

Average speed = total distance/total time = 2d/(3d/10) = 20/3 = 6.66667 ~ 6.67 Km/hr
